title: Static desktop bearer-token authentication for the inbound boundary (desktop -> plane), mirroring the outbound Foundry development API key

supersedesEarlierDesign.note: An earlier draft of this task restricted the scheme to Development and Test, mirroring DevelopmentFoundryApiKeyAuthenticator exactly. The operator redirected mid-task: this application will never have an Entra app registration in ANY environment, so the mechanism had to be a real, explicitly opt-in PRODUCTION path rather than a development-only stand-in. The implementation below reflects the corrected design; the environment-guard constructor and its tests were replaced, not layered on top of.

mechanism.optInGate: SupportPlaneOptions.StaticDesktopTokenEnabled (config key Sapphirus:StaticDesktopTokenEnabled), defaults to false in every environment including Production.
mechanism.whenFalse: AddJwtBearer is the only registered scheme and the default authenticate scheme, byte-identical to the behaviour before this feature existed.
mechanism.whenTrue: DesktopAuthenticationComposition additionally registers StaticDesktopAuthenticationHandler under scheme name SapphirusStaticDesktopToken and makes it the default authenticate scheme. AddJwtBearer stays registered, unconditionally, alongside it -- Program.cs never conditionally skips it.
mechanism.environmentGuard: None. This is the deliberate change from the superseded design: the mechanism must be usable in Production because this operator will never hold Entra app-registration rights in any environment for this application.
mechanism.failClosedBoundary: StaticDesktopTokenAuthenticator is constructed eagerly and synchronously inside AddDesktopAuthentication -- not behind a lazily-resolved DI factory -- so a missing, too-short, too-long, denylisted-placeholder, or all-one-character token throws static_desktop_token_invalid immediately at host composition, before WebApplication.Build() returns.
mechanism.startupLog: Program.cs logs a single warning after builder.Build() when options.StaticDesktopTokenEnabled is true: the fact that the mechanism is active, and the two words identifying it (Sapphirus:StaticDesktopTokenEnabled=true), never the token, never any claim value.

tokenHardening.characterRule: bounded printable ASCII, 0x21-0x7E, identical rule to DevelopmentFoundryApiKeyAuthenticator
tokenHardening.repeatedCharacterRejection: A token of one character repeated across its full length is rejected even at a legal length (e.g. 40 copies of 'a').
tokenHardening.comparison: CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals over UTF-8 bytes; a length mismatch is rejected before that call, which the API requires (FixedTimeEquals needs equal-length spans) and which leaks nothing about content, only that lengths differed.
neverExposed: Not logged: HandleAuthenticateAsync's failure path uses a fixed string, 'The static desktop token was not accepted.', never the presented or configured value.
Not in telemetry: no telemetry call site in this feature references the token or the authenticator.
Not in a problem document: the 401 challenge produced by ASP.NET Core's authentication middleware carries no application-authored body from this feature.
Not in a health response: no health check in this repository was changed or references this mechanism.
Not in a receipt: ModelResultGuards and the receipt types were not touched by this feature.

subjectDesign.chosen: Prefer an explicitly configured Sapphirus:StaticDesktopSubjectId (a Guid in 'D' format, validated at SupportPlaneOptions.Validate time). When absent, derive deterministically: "static-" + SHA256("sapphirus:static-desktop-subject:v1\n" + token)[..32] (hex).
subjectDesign.why: The rate limiter partition, IIdempotencyStore.ExecuteAsync(subject, key, ...), per-subject consent consumption, IDeviceRegistry.FindActiveAsync(subject, registrationId), and the receipt SubjectHash ModelResultGuards checks all require a subject stable across requests and restarts. An explicit id gives an operator direct control in a multi-desktop deployment; the fallback keeps single-desktop deployments working with zero extra configuration.
subjectDesign.nonReversibility: SHA-256 is one-way; the token cannot be recovered from the derived subject.
subjectDesign.stability: Depends only on the configured token, which does not change between restarts of the same deployment, so the derived subject -- and therefore every partition and idempotency key built from it -- is stable across restarts.
subjectDesign.neverTheTokenItself: Verified by test (Two_authenticators_built_from_the_same_token_derive_the_same_subject asserts the derived oid never contains the token as a substring).

evidenceDistinguishability.requestTimePrincipal: Every principal built by this mechanism carries claim sapphirus_static_token_principal = "true", which a real Entra token never has. The derived subject additionally carries a static- prefix, which can never collide with a real Entra oid (always a bare GUID).
evidenceDistinguishability.namedGap: There is no equivalent of the outbound CredentialMechanismId-folded-into-CredentialBindingHash (FND-030) on the inbound side. ModelAccessReceiptV2's TenantHash and SubjectHash are opaque SHA-256 digests of the tenant and subject (ScopeAuthorization.SubjectPartition), computed identically regardless of which authentication mechanism produced the principal. Folding the inbound mechanism into the receipt would require adding a field to ModelAccessReceiptV2, updating ModelResultGuards.ValidateReceiptV2, and moving the cross-language receipt digest fixture in lockstep -- a receipt-schema change outside this task's lease and outside its scope (authentication, not receipt shape). Recorded here rather than attempted speculatively.

authorizationUnchanged.claim: ScopeAuthorization.IsApprovedDesktopPrincipal is byte-identical to before this feature. Confirmed by diff and by test: the static principal is checked against it directly, with no override, no bypass, and no widened predicate.
authorizationUnchanged.provenGenuine: StaticDesktopTokenAuthenticator.GrantedScopes deliberately withholds DesktopScopes.DiagnosticsUpload. The_principal_is_refused_a_scope_it_was_not_granted asserts IsApprovedDesktopPrincipal returns false for that scope against the real static principal, and A_principal_from_an_unapproved_client_is_still_refused asserts the azp/appid check is genuinely evaluated by rebuilding the principal against a support-plane configuration with a different approved client.

requiredEnvironmentVariablesForAWorkingP: Sapphirus__Authority = https://login.microsoftonline.com/<any syntactically valid tenant GUID>/v2.0 -- required because AddJwtBearer is always registered and SupportPlaneOptions.Validate demands a well-formed Authority regardless of which scheme is default; it never needs to be a real, reachable tenant when the static mechanism is what actually authenticates requests.

Sapphirus__ApprovedDesktopClientId = <any syntactically valid GUID> -- becomes the azp/appid the static principal presents, so it is also the value ScopeAuthorization.IsApprovedDesktopPrincipal checks against.
Sapphirus__StaticDesktopToken = <a long, random, operator-generated token, at least 32 printable ASCII characters, not a placeholder, not a single repeated character>
Sapphirus__StaticDesktopSubjectId = <optional Guid 'D' format; omit to use the deterministic derivation>

unverifiable: No live desktop client build was run against this mechanism end-to-end; the end-to-end proof is the in-process WebApplicationFactory<Program> test hitting the real ASP.NET Core pipeline (real authentication middleware, real DesktopAuthenticationComposition, real ScopeAuthorization), not the packaged Windows desktop app.

The claim that a future Entra rollout needs zero code changes beyond leaving the flag false is a structural argument (AddJwtBearer's registration and options never depend on StaticDesktopTokenEnabled), not something a test can execute without a real Entra tenant.
